brief: The note answers ten questions on the 2026 bond sell-off. Yields hit multi-year highs since July but rose more slowly (30-55bp) than after the US-Iran war (55-90bp), so this is not panic, though levels raise debt-sustainability concerns. Energy tensions (Middle East, Russian refining) pushed inflation and rate expectations (Fed +35bp, ECB +50bp) higher, the dominant driver. Stable swap spreads argue against fiscal concerns as the cause. AI credit issuance ($356bn ytd) is now half of Treasury net supply, but swap spreads show no strong crowding out. Bessent's buybacks and TGA measures are accounting tricks that could backfire if intensified. Only fiscal consolidation helps, and midterms likely bring deadlock plus modest 0.5-0.6% of GDP consolidation, not stabilization. Warsh's Jackson Hole reassurance calmed markets, and the Fed would only intervene if functioning were at risk. The debasement trade (weaker dollar, gold, Bitcoin) has returned, less intensely than in 2025. European political instability widens French and Italian spreads, and BoJ hikes risk pulling global yields higher via Japanese repatriation. Outlook: self-fulfilling spikes up to 70bp are possible, but risks are balanced since any demand shock would quickly lower yields.
